Kagiso Rabada & Lungi Ngidi - The Proteas Hunting Pair

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet the spearheads of the Proteas bowling attack: Kagiso Rabada & Lungi Ngidi

Unique Selling Point:
One of the most exciting aspects of the Proteas cricket team has been the rise to prominence of Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi.

Tonight on Carte Blanche, we shine a spotlight on the twin spearheads of the Proteas bowling attack. Throughout history, great fast bowlers have hunted in pairs: Lillee & Thompson, Wasim & Waqar, Andersson & Broad, Donald & Pollock

However nothing is as exciting as the prospect of KG & Lungi Ngidi leading the Proteas attack over the next 5-7 years.

Not only are they supremely talented but they showcase a Proteas team that is not only amongst the best in the world but truly representative of all South Africa.


Summary:
Kagiso Rabada & Lungi Ngidi look set to lead the Proteas bowling attack for the foreseeable future. For the first time in South African history, the national cricket team will be spearheaded by 2 black men, chosen purely on merit.

23 year old Kagiso is the 2nd ranked by the ICC test bowler in the world currentl, while 21 year old Lungi burst onto the scene taking 6 wickets in his debut match against India last year.

For a country that has struggled with the aspect of transformation in sport since the end of Apartheid, these two young men are role models for a new generation of cricketers to aspire to and emulate.

In this episode of Carte Blanche we look back on their very different journeys to national stardom.

Kagiso's dad is a doctor and his mum is a lawyer. He attended the prestigious Saint Stithians School and announced his talent by leading the South African u19 team to a world cup win in 2014

Lungi's parents were domestic workers. Their employers paid for Lungi to attend Hilton College in KZN where his cricket talent was nurtured.

Apart from interviewing both men, we will chat to:

Kagiso's Mom & Dad

Lungi's Mother

Lungi's cricket coach at Hilton, Sean Carlisle

We will also interview prominent cricket commentator Aslam Khota

We will try to secure interviews with Faf Du Plessis (Proteas Captain) and Otis Gibson (Proteas coach)

Press Release:


From Lillee and Thomson; Wasim and Waqar; and Donald and Pollock - throughout history, great bowlers have hunted in pairs. In South Africa, the young, powerful combination of Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi form part of the Proteas’ bowling attack. One is currently the best bowler in the world and the other is considered one of best cricketers in the country. But as Ngidi sits out the tournament against Pakistan because of injury, could these extraordinary youngsters become cricket’s ‘next great hunting pair’?

Script:


INTRO VOICE OVER: In cricket there’s nothing quite like raw pace. A bowler hurling a missile at up to 150km/h certainly gets the adrenalin pumping, from the batsmen, to the crowds who flock to see such spectacles, to the kids who idolise heroes like Donald, Pollock, Ntini & Steyn

Derek Intro Link: This is the bullring at the Wanderers in Johannesburg and when these covers come off, it’s a fast and testing wicket and our bowlers have intimidated the best batsmen in the world over the past 3 decades. But now there are 2 young fast bowlers who look set to spearhead the Proteas attack and write the next chapter of South African cricket.

Kagiso Rabada & Lungi Ngidi are two of the most exciting bowlers in South Africa right now, both blessed with the ability to bowl at express pace.

KG is currently terrorizing the touring Pakistani batsmen but Lungi is out injured, yet both are important components of the Proteas’ vaunted pace battery.
Their journey from obscurity to national heroes couldn’t be more different.
V/O: Since his debut in 2015, 23-year old KG has enjoyed a meteoric rise to fame becoming the top test bowler in the world.

Raised in the affluent Johannesburg suburb of Bryanston, KG discovered his love of cricket almost by accident

KG on discovering cricket by accident

V/O: He attended the prestigious Saint Stithians College where his raw potential was immediately noticed by director of cricket Wim Jansen

Comment from Wim Jansen




V/O: To bowl fast is one of the rarest commodities in cricket. Vincent Barnes is High Performance Centre manager and a former Proteas bowling coach. When he saw KG for the first time, he couldn’t help but get excited.

Comments from Vincent


V/O: KG wasn’t the only promising bowler blessed with pace. A world away from the leafy suburbs of Johannesburg in the KZN Midlands, Lungisani Ngidi hails from much humbler origins.

Lungi tells us his background and how he fell in love with cricket

V/O: Lungi’s sporting prowess saw him earn a scholarship at the illustrious Hilton College where Dale Benkenstein is now head coach

Beat about self-belief and the dream about becoming a Protea
V/O: While Lungi dreamt of becoming a Protea, that dream became reality for KG in 2015

KG on his dream of becoming a Protea

V/O: Since that debut, KG ‘s taken the world by storm. In just 34 tests he’s taken 163 wickets at an astounding strike rate of a wicket every 38,5 balls – the best in South African history.

This country is a nursery for exceptional fast bowlers. Radio Commentator Aslam Kota has witnessed many of them first hand.

Aslam and Vincent talk about KG’s achievements.
V/O: Not to be outdone Lungi announced himself in spectacular style by taking 7 wickets on debut and earning the man of the match award against India, the best test side in the world.

Derek Link: In 1990 South Africa was welcomed back to world cricket after decades in isolation. There was a vision then that South African cricket could only go from strength to strength because of the inclusion of all races in the country. Now 29 years later, with the likes of KG & Lungi in the team, has that dream come true?
V/O: These days the Proteas boast a 4-pronged pace battery that some say rivals the great West Indian attack of the 1980’s.

As veterans like Dale Steyn and Vernon Philander enter the twilight of their career, it will soon be up to both KG & Lungi to inherit the mantle of leaders of the attack.

Their continued success will inspire millions of kids all into believing they too could one day represent their country and perhaps even exceed the accomplishments of their heroes.
